usage.financial_condition: Insolvency is a financial or legally defined condition involving inability to pay debts or an unfavorable relationship between liabilities and assets.

usage.legal_tests: Legal systems may apply a cash-flow test, a balance-sheet test, or another statutory test; the controlling definition depends on jurisdiction and context.
usage.cash_flow: Cash-flow insolvency generally concerns inability to pay debts as they become due.
usage.balance_sheet: Balance-sheet insolvency generally concerns liabilities exceeding assets under the applicable valuation rules.
usage.bankruptcy_contrast: Insolvency is a condition, whereas bankruptcy ordinarily refers to a formal legal proceeding or status.
usage.liquidation_contrast: An insolvent company may enter liquidation, restructuring, administration, or another procedure; insolvency does not itself mean that liquidation has occurred.
usage.person_company: Both individuals and organizations can be insolvent, although the available legal procedures and terminology vary.

nuance.ja: insolvency は、債務者の「財務状態」を表し、正式な破産・清算手続きそのものではない。代表的な考え方には、期限の到来した債務を支払えるかを見る cash-flow insolvency と、一定の評価方法で負債が資産を上回るかを見る balance-sheet insolvency がある。ただし、具体的な定義・評価対象・時点・推定規定は法域や法令によって異なる。したがって、手元資金が一時的に不足しただけで常に法的な insolvency に該当するとも、資産総額が負債を上回っていれば必ず solvent であるとも限らない。bankruptcy は通常、申立てや命令を伴う正式な法的手続き・地位である。liquidation は資産の換価・債務処理・事業終了を進める手続きであり、insolvency の結果として選ばれることはあるが、両者は同義ではない。会社が insolvency に直面しても、再建・債務整理・資金注入などによって事業を継続できる場合がある。
nuance.en: Insolvency describes a debtor’s financial condition rather than the formal bankruptcy or liquidation procedure itself. Common approaches include cash-flow insolvency, which concerns whether debts can be paid as they become due, and balance-sheet insolvency, which concerns whether liabilities exceed assets under applicable valuation rules. The exact definition, valuation method, relevant date, and statutory presumptions differ among jurisdictions and legal contexts. A temporary shortage of readily available cash therefore does not invariably establish legal insolvency, and assets exceeding liabilities do not necessarily establish an ability to pay debts when due. Bankruptcy ordinarily denotes a formal legal proceeding or status involving a petition, order, or similar act. Liquidation is a procedure for realizing assets, settling liabilities, and often ending a business. It may result from insolvency but is not synonymous with it. A company facing insolvency may sometimes continue through restructuring, debt arrangements, or additional financing.

ja: insolvency：債務を期限どおり支払えない、または一定の基準で負債が資産を上回る財務状態。

liquidation：資産を換価し、債務を処理して、通常は会社の業務を終了させる手続き。
default：期限までに特定の債務・契約上の義務を履行しないこと。
illiquidity：保有資産があっても、直ちに利用できる現金が不足している状態。
financial distress：債務返済や事業継続に困難が生じている広い財務危機状態。
solvency：債務を履行できる支払能力、または資産・負債関係が健全な状態。
restructuring：債務・事業・資本構成などを再編して財務状態の改善を図ること。
en: insolvency is a financial condition involving inability to pay debts or liabilities exceeding assets under a relevant test.
bankruptcy is a formal legal proceeding or status for dealing with debts that cannot be paid.
liquidation realizes assets and settles liabilities, commonly in connection with ending a company’s affairs.
default is failure to perform a particular debt or contractual obligation when it becomes due.
illiquidity is a shortage of immediately available cash despite the possible ownership of valuable assets.
financial distress is the broader condition of difficulty meeting obligations or continuing business.
solvency is the ability to meet debts or a financially sound relationship between assets and liabilities.
restructuring reorganizes debts, operations, or capital to improve financial viability.

etymology.ja: insolvency は insolvent に状態を表す接尾辞 -cy が付いて成立した。insolvent はラテン語 insolvens に由来し、否定を表す in- と solvere「解く、解放する、支払う」から成る。solvere は、拘束を「解く」ことから、債務を支払って義務関係を解消する意味を発達させた。したがって insolvent は文字どおりには「支払って解決することができない」、insolvency はその状態を表す。solvent、solvency、solve、solution も歴史的には同じ語族に属する。
etymology.en: Insolvency was formed from insolvent with the state-forming suffix -cy. Insolvent derives from Latin insolvens and combines the negative prefix in- with solvere, to loosen, release, or pay. Solvere developed the financial sense of discharging a debt and thereby releasing the debtor from the obligation. Insolvent therefore literally represents being unable to pay and discharge an obligation, while insolvency denotes that condition. Solvent, solvency, solve, and solution belong historically to the same word family.

nuance.ja: cost of living は、単に一世帯が実際に支払った金額ではなく、特定の場所・時期に一定の生活水準を維持するために必要となる一般的な費用水準を表す。living expenses は個人や家庭の具体的な支出項目に焦点を置きやすいのに対し、cost of living は東京と地方、現在と前年などを比較する経済的な尺度としても使われる。standard of living は、所得・住宅・医療・教育・余暇などを含む生活の物質的水準であり、その生活を維持する費用とは異なる。inflation は物価全般の継続的な上昇を表し、cost of living の上昇を引き起こし得るが、両者は完全な同義語ではない。a cost-of-living adjustment は、生活費の変化に応じて賃金・年金・給付などを調整することで、しばしば COLA と略される。
nuance.en: Cost of living does not merely mean the amount one household happened to spend. It describes the general expense required to maintain a given way or standard of life in a particular place and period. Living expenses more readily refers to the specific bills and expenditures of an individual or household, whereas cost of living also functions as an economic basis for comparing cities, countries, or time periods. Standard of living describes the material quality or level of life, including income, housing, healthcare, education, and leisure, rather than the expense required to sustain it. Inflation is a continuing general increase in prices and may raise the cost of living, but the terms are not identical. A cost-of-living adjustment changes wages, pensions, or benefits in response to changing living costs and is often abbreviated to COLA.

etymology.ja: cost は古フランス語 cost、現代フランス語 coût に関係し、ラテン語 constare「一定の価格である、成り立つ」にさかのぼる。constare は con-「ともに」と stare「立つ」から成り、価格が確定しているという意味を発達させた。living は古英語 libban「生きる」に由来する live の動名詞・名詞形である。cost of living は文字どおりには「生活することの費用」であり、近代的な物価・賃金・家計の統計が発達するにつれて、一定の生活水準を維持するために必要な費用を表す経済用語として定着した。
etymology.en: Cost came through Old French cost and is related to modern French coût, ultimately deriving from Latin constare, to stand at a fixed price or consist. Constare combines con-, together, with stare, to stand, and developed the idea of an established price. Living is derived from live, from Old English libban, to be alive. Cost of living therefore literally means the expense of living. As modern statistics concerning prices, wages, and household budgets developed, the phrase became established as an economic term for the amount required to maintain a particular standard of life.

nuance.ja: economics は語末に -s があるが、学問名としては通常、単数扱いとなり Economics is ... とする。economy が現実の生産・消費・雇用・取引から成る「経済」そのものを表すのに対し、economics はその仕組みを研究する「経済学」である。microeconomics は個人・家庭・企業・特定市場の選択や価格形成を、macroeconomics は経済全体の成長・物価・失業・金融政策・財政政策などを扱う。the economics of a project と言う場合は学問一般ではなく、その事業の費用構造・予想収益・誘因・採算性を意味する。この用法では、技術的に実現可能でも the economics do not work のように、費用に見合わず事業として成立しないことを表せる。ただし、学問名としての基本的な一致は単数である。
nuance.en: Although economics ends in -s, it normally takes singular agreement as the name of an academic discipline: Economics is a social science. Economy denotes the actual system of production, consumption, employment, and exchange, whereas economics is the field that studies how that system operates. Microeconomics examines the choices and interactions of individuals, households, firms, and particular markets. Macroeconomics examines economy-wide matters such as growth, inflation, unemployment, monetary policy, and fiscal policy. In the economics of a project, the word refers not to the discipline generally but to the project’s cost structure, expected revenue, incentives, and commercial viability. In this specialized use, the economics do not work can mean that something is technically possible but not financially sustainable. The discipline itself nevertheless normally takes a singular verb.

etymology.ja: economics は economy に学問分野を表す -ics が付いて成立した。economy はギリシャ語 oikonomia「家政、家の管理」に由来し、oikos「家、世帯」と、nomos「規則、管理」または nemein「配分する、管理する」に関係する要素から成る。もとは世帯の財産・食料・労働などを管理することを意味したが、後に国家・社会全体の生産・交換・資源配分へ対象が広がった。economics は、そのような経済活動の法則と仕組みを体系的に研究する学問の名称となった。
etymology.en: Economics was formed from economy with -ics, a suffix used in the names of fields of study. Economy derives from Greek oikonomia, household management, combining oikos, house or household, with an element related to nomos, rule or management, and nemein, to distribute or administer. The original concept concerned managing a household’s property, food, and labor. Its scope later expanded to the production, exchange, and allocation of resources throughout a state or society. Economics consequently became the name of the systematic discipline studying the mechanisms and principles of such activity.

note.ja: 経済現象を体系的・科学的に研究する分野であることを明示する形式的な表現。

nuance.ja: interest rate は、元本に対して一定期間に発生する利息の割合である。借り手にとっては借入費用、預金者・投資家にとっては資金を提供することで得る収益率となる。単に five percent と表示されていても、それが年率か月率か、固定か変動か、単利か複利か、手数料を含むかを確認しなければ実際の負担は分からない。fixed interest rate は一定期間変わらない金利、variable または floating interest rate は指標などに応じて変動する金利を表す。nominal interest rate は通常、物価変動を調整していない名目金利で、real interest rate はインフレの影響を考慮した実質金利である。APR は借入費用を比較するための年率表示だが、その法的定義と含まれる費用は制度によって異なり、単純な契約金利と同一とは限らない。
nuance.en: An interest rate is the proportion of principal that accrues as interest over a specified period. For a borrower it represents part of the cost of obtaining credit, while for a depositor or investor it represents a return for supplying funds. A quotation of five percent alone does not reveal the actual cost unless one knows whether the period is annual or monthly, whether the rate is fixed or variable, whether interest is simple or compounded, and whether fees are included. A fixed interest rate remains unchanged for an agreed period, whereas a variable or floating rate changes according to an index or other mechanism. A nominal interest rate normally does not adjust for changes in prices, while a real interest rate takes inflation into account. APR is an annualized measure intended to assist comparison of borrowing costs, but its legal definition and included charges vary and it is not necessarily identical to the contractual interest rate.

etymology.en: Interest derives from Latin interesse, to be between, matter, or concern, combining inter-, between, with esse, to be. Rate is related to medieval Latin rata, a calculated proportion, ultimately from Latin reri, to calculate or consider. Interest rate therefore denotes the calculated proportion between interest and the principal on which it accrues.

nuance.ja: neither は、原則として二つの選択肢の両方を否定する。neither answer は「二つの答えのどちらも～ない」、neither of the answers は「その二つの答えのどちらも～ない」を意味する。三つ以上をまとめて否定する場合は none of が自然である。ただし、日常英語では二つを厳密に意識せず neither が使われる場合もある。neither ... nor ... は両方を否定する対句で、Neither the buyer nor the seller was ready. のように用いる。二つの主語の数が異なる場合、動詞は近い方の主語に一致させることが多いが、不自然さや曖昧さを避けるため文を書き換えることも望ましい。否定文への同意では Neither do I. のように助動詞と主語を倒置する。Me neither. は非常に自然だが口語的である。
nuance.en: Neither normally excludes both of two alternatives. Neither answer means not either of two answers, while neither of the answers refers explicitly to the two answers as a group. None of is normally preferred when three or more items are being excluded, although everyday usage does not always observe the numerical distinction strictly. Neither ... nor ... creates a paired negative structure, as in Neither the buyer nor the seller was ready. When coordinated subjects differ in number, the verb often agrees with the nearer subject, but rewriting the sentence may avoid awkwardness or ambiguity. In response to a negative statement, neither takes auxiliary–subject inversion: Neither do I. Me neither is extremely natural in conversation but more informal.

nuance.ja: whichever は、文脈上分かっている複数の選択肢から「どれを選んでも」「実際に選ばれるどれか」を表す。Choose whichever seat you like. なら、利用可能な座席の中から好きなものを選べる。either は原則として二つのうちどちらかを指すが、whichever は二つに限定されず、三つ以上の選択肢にも使える。which は話者が選択肢を尋ねる語であるのに対し、whichever は選択を相手に委ねたり、どの選択でも結果が同じであることを示したりする。whatever は対象の範囲が明示されていない場合にも使える、より広い語である。Whichever comes first や whichever is earlier は、契約・規則・日程説明で二つ以上の基準のうち最初に成立するものを指定する便利な表現である。
nuance.en: Whichever refers to any alternative selected from a group understood from context or to the particular alternative that ultimately applies. usage.policy_sense: Reflation can mean deliberate monetary or fiscal stimulation intended to raise demand, output, employment, and the price level after weakness or deflation.

usage.inflation_contrast: Reflation is generally a recovery from deficient demand or abnormally low prices and does not necessarily mean uncontrolled or excessive inflation.
usage.policy_tools: Depending on context, reflationary measures may include lower interest rates, increased money or credit availability, tax reductions, or higher government spending.

nuance.ja: reflation は、単に物価が上昇する inflation と異なり、景気低迷・需要不足・デフレなどによって低下した経済活動や物価水準を、政策によって回復させるという意味を持つ。金融政策では金利引下げや資金供給の拡大、財政政策では政府支出の増加や減税などが reflationary measures となり得る。狭い技術的用法では、物価水準が長期的な傾向線を下回った後、その水準へ戻ることを指す。したがって、reflation は通常、デフレからの正常化または景気回復の初期段階として肯定的・中立的に語られ、直ちに制御不能なインフレを意味しない。ただし刺激が過度または長期化すれば、望ましい回復を超えて高インフレへつながる可能性はある。金融市場の reflation trade は、成長・物価・金利の上昇を見込んで、それによって利益を得やすい資産へ投資する戦略を表す。
nuance.en: Unlike inflation, which simply denotes a rise in the general price level, reflation carries the idea of restoring economic activity and prices after recession, deficient demand, or deflation. Lower interest rates and increased liquidity may serve as monetary reflationary measures, while greater government spending or tax reductions may provide fiscal reflation. In a narrower technical sense, reflation is the recovery of a price level that has fallen below its longer-term trend. It is therefore often presented neutrally or positively as normalization following deflation or as an early phase of recovery and does not automatically imply excessive or uncontrolled inflation. If stimulus becomes too strong or persists too long, however, the recovery may develop into undesirably high inflation. In financial markets, a reflation trade is a strategy designed to benefit from expectations of stronger growth, rising prices, and often higher interest rates.

etymology.ja: reflation は re-「再び、元へ」と inflation から作られた経済用語である。inflation はラテン語 inflare「吹き込む、膨らませる」に由来し、in-「中へ」と flare「吹く」から成る。経済上の inflation が通貨量や物価水準の膨張を表すようになった後、低下した価格・需要・経済活動を再び膨らませ、以前の水準へ戻す政策または過程を表すため reflation が形成された。したがって、語の構造上も単なる継続的な物価上昇より「再び膨らませる」という回復の意味が強い。
etymology.en: Reflation was formed from re-, again or back, and inflation. Inflation derives from Latin inflare, to blow into or expand, combining in-, into, with flare, to blow. After inflation became an economic term for expansion in money or the price level, reflation was created to describe deliberately expanding depressed demand, prices, or activity again and restoring them toward an earlier or desired path. Its structure therefore emphasizes renewed expansion or recovery rather than an indefinite continuation of rising prices.

nuance.ja: reflationary は、景気後退・需要不足・デフレなどの後に、経済活動と物価水準を回復させる政策・圧力・環境を表す。reflationary monetary policy なら、金利引下げや資金供給の拡大などによって需要と物価を押し上げる金融政策、reflationary fiscal policy なら、政府支出の増加や減税による刺激策を意味する。inflationary は物価上昇を引き起こすものを広く表し、その物価上昇が望ましいか過度かを問わない。これに対し reflationary は、低迷した経済や低すぎる物価を正常な軌道へ戻すという回復的な含みを持つ。ただし、reflationary policy が予想以上に強く作用すれば、過度な inflationary pressure を生む可能性もある。投資の文脈では、reflationary trade や reflationary strategy が、成長・物価・金利の上昇から利益を得ることを狙う取引を表す。
nuance.en: Reflationary describes a policy, pressure, or environment that restores economic activity and prices after recession, deficient demand, or deflation. Reflationary monetary policy may involve lower interest rates or increased liquidity intended to strengthen demand and prices. Reflationary fiscal policy may involve increased government spending or tax reductions. Inflationary broadly describes anything causing prices to rise, without indicating whether the increase is a desirable recovery or an excessive development. Reflationary, by contrast, carries the restorative implication of returning a depressed economy or an abnormally low price level toward a more normal path. A reflationary policy that proves stronger than expected may nevertheless generate excessive inflationary pressure. In investment language, a reflationary trade or strategy seeks to benefit from rising growth, prices, and often interest rates.

nuance.ja: cope with は、困難な状況を完全に解決・克服するというより、その負担に耐えながら何とか機能し続けることを表す。She coped with the pressure. は、圧力そのものを取り除いたのではなく、その状況下でも必要な行動ができたという意味である。deal with は問題への対応全般を表し、解決の成否を問わない場合もある。handle は状況を管理・処理できる能力に焦点を置き、cope with より自信のある響きになりやすい。overcome は困難に打ち勝ち、障害を乗り越えるという、より完全な成功を示す。感情・病気・喪失などについて cope with を使うときは、その人が弱いと断定するのではなく、継続的な適応過程を表せる。否定形 can’t cope は、負担が能力を超えているという強い表現になり得る。
nuance.en: Cope with generally means continuing to function under a difficult burden rather than completely solving or defeating it. The negative can’t cope may strongly suggest that the demands of the situation have exceeded someone’s present capacity.

etymology.ja: cope は中期英語 copen「争う、立ち向かう」に由来し、古フランス語 couper「打つ」と関係すると考えられている。初期には敵と戦う、打ち合うという意味を持ち、そこから困難な相手・状況に立ち向かう意味へ発達した。後に with を伴って、問題・圧力・変化などに対処し、何とか切り抜けるという現代的な cope with の用法が定着した。
etymology.en: Cope derives from Middle English copen, to contend or encounter, and is generally connected with Old French couper, to strike. Its earlier meanings involved fighting or meeting an opponent in combat. The word then developed the figurative sense of confronting and managing a difficult situation. With subsequently became established as the preposition introducing the problem, pressure, or change being managed, producing the modern construction cope with.

nuance.ja: 動詞 handle の中心は、対象を手の内に置き、適切に扱うことである。物理的に物を「手で扱う」という意味から、問題・仕事・人物・情報などを管理・処理する意味へ広がった。I can handle it. は、単に問題へ対応するだけでなく、「自分に任せてよい、対処する能力がある」という自信を表す。cope with は困難な負担に耐えながら何とか機能することを強調するのに対し、handle は状況を制御し、必要な処理を行う能力を感じさせやすい。handle a person は「その人にうまく対処する」を意味するが、人を物のように管理する響きになることもある。名詞の get a handle on は、複雑な問題を理解・制御できる段階へ到達することを表す。SNSなどの handle は、他の利用者がその人を識別するためのユーザー名である。
nuance.en: The core idea of handle is bringing something under one’s hand and dealing with it appropriately. The physical meaning of touching or manipulating an object developed into the figurative sense of managing problems, tasks, people, and information. I can handle it expresses not merely willingness to respond but confidence that the speaker has the capacity to take control of the matter. Cope with emphasizes continuing to function under difficulty or stress, whereas handle more readily suggests competence, control, and effective processing. Handle a person can mean deal effectively with them, but it may sound as though the person is being managed like an object. The noun phrase get a handle on means reach a sufficient level of understanding or control. On social media, a handle is a username by which other users identify an account.

The physical idea was then extended metaphorically to bringing a problem, task, person, or body of information under one’s control. nuance.ja: bear with は、相手に不便・待ち時間・分かりにくい説明などを一時的に我慢してもらう表現である。Bear with me for a moment. は、話者が情報を確認する、考えをまとめる、操作を終えるなどの間、少し待ってほしいという丁寧な依頼になる。Please wait. よりも、「こちらの事情でご不便をかけるが、辛抱してほしい」という含みがある。If you’ll bear with me, ... は、説明が長い、または一見本題から外れて見えるものの、最後には意味が分かるので聞き続けてほしいときにも使われる。put up with は不快な人・状況を嫌々耐える否定的な響きが強いが、bear with は通常、一時的な状況に対して協力と忍耐を求める比較的丁寧な表現である。
nuance.en: Bear with asks another person to tolerate a temporary inconvenience, delay, or difficult explanation. Bear with me for a moment politely requests patience while the speaker checks information, organizes a thought, or completes a task. Compared with Please wait, it more clearly acknowledges that the speaker’s circumstances may inconvenience the listener and asks for cooperation. If you’ll bear with me can also introduce a long or apparently indirect explanation whose relevance will become clear later. Put up with often suggests reluctantly tolerating a persistently unpleasant person or situation, whereas bear with usually requests cooperative patience during a temporary difficulty.

etymology.ja: bear は古英語 beran「運ぶ、担う、支える、耐える」に由来し、ドイツ語 tragen などと意味上比較できる古いゲルマン系の動詞である。物理的な重さを担う意味から、苦痛・困難・負担に耐える意味が発達した。bear with では、相手の遅れ・不完全さ・長い説明などを一時的な負担として受け止め、忍耐を保つという比喩的な意味になる。過去形は bore、過去分詞は borne であり、出生に用いる born とは区別される。
etymology.en: Bear comes from Old English beran, to carry, support, produce, or endure, and belongs to an old Germanic family of verbs involving carrying or bearing. The physical sense of carrying a weight developed into enduring pain, difficulty, or another burden. In bear with, a person’s delay, imperfection, or extended explanation is figuratively treated as a temporary burden that the listener patiently carries. The past tense is bore and the past participle in this sense is borne, which is distinct from born in expressions concerning birth.

usage.that_clause: Bear in mind that introduces a fact, limitation, or warning that should influence thought or action.
usage.noun_position: A short noun or pronoun commonly appears between bear and in mind: bear this in mind.
usage.long_object: A longer object or clause commonly follows the complete phrase: bear in mind the practical difficulties; bear in mind that costs may rise.

usage.memory_and_consideration: The phrase can mean remember, but usually suggests actively considering the information when deciding or acting.

en: to remember an important fact, condition, or warning
to consider a particular circumstance when making a decision, plan, or judgment
to keep information consciously available because it will be relevant later
to ask someone to take account of an important limitation, exception, or caution

nuance.ja: bear in mind は、単に過去の情報を記憶しているだけでなく、その情報を現在または将来の判断・行動に反映させることを表す。Bear in mind that the deadline is Friday. は、金曜日という期限を覚えるだけでなく、作業計画をそれに合わせるよう促している。remember は情報を忘れないこと、consider はある事項について考えることを広く表す。take into account は複数の事情を評価・計算・判断へ具体的に組み入れる、より分析的な表現である。keep in mind は bear in mind とほぼ同義だが、やや会話的である。形式的な文章では It should be borne in mind that ... が使われるが、冗長に響くこともあるため、The court should consider that ... のように具体的な主語と動詞へ書き換えると明確になる場合がある。
nuance.en: Bear in mind means more than retaining information in memory; it usually requires allowing that information to influence a present or future decision or action. Bear in mind that the deadline is Friday asks the listener not only to remember the date but also to plan accordingly. Remember focuses on not forgetting information, while consider broadly means thinking about a matter. Take into account is more analytical and suggests incorporating a factor into an evaluation, calculation, or decision. Keep in mind is nearly synonymous with bear in mind but is somewhat more conversational. Formal writing sometimes uses It should be borne in mind that ..., although a direct construction such as The court should consider that ... may be clearer.

etymology.ja: bear は古英語 beran「運ぶ、担う、支える」に由来し、mind は古英語 gemynd「記憶、思考、心」にさかのぼる。bear something in mind は、ある事実や考えを心の中に「携えておく、保持する」という比喩に基づく。物理的な荷物を運ぶ bear が、責任・感情・考えなどを精神的に保持する意味へ広がった。過去形は bore、過去分詞は borne であり、受動形では It should be borne in mind. となる。
etymology.en: Bear comes from Old English beran, to carry, support, or sustain, while mind derives from Old English gemynd, memory, thought, or the faculty of thinking. Bear something in mind is based on the metaphor of carrying or retaining a fact or idea within one’s mind. The physical verb bear thus extended to the mental retention of a responsibility, feeling, or consideration. Its past tense is bore and its past participle is borne, producing the formal passive expression It should be borne in mind.

usage.maximum: Up to before a number expresses a maximum and normally includes that number: up to ten people means no more than ten.
usage.no_guaranteed_minimum: Up to states a ceiling but does not by itself guarantee any particular minimum.
usage.time: Up to can mean until a time or stage: up to the present; events leading up to the meeting.
usage.distance_level: It can indicate movement or extent as far as a place, person, level, or boundary.
usage.responsibility: Be up to someone means that the person has the responsibility or authority to decide.
usage.activity: Be up to something can mean be doing or planning something, often something secret, surprising, or possibly improper.
usage.ability: Not be up to something means lack sufficient strength, health, ability, or willingness for it.
usage.standard: Up to a standard means reaching the required level, commonly in be up to standard.
usage.gerund: After to in this expression, use a noun or gerund rather than an infinitive: Are you up to walking home?

nuance.ja: up to は文脈によって意味が大きく変わる。up to ten people は「最大10人」で、通常10を含むが、10人参加することを保証せず、0人から10人までの可能性がある。It’s up to you. は「あなた次第です」「決定はあなたに任されています」を意味する。What are you up to? は中立的に「何をしているの」と尋ねる場合も、何かを企んでいると疑う場合もある。I’m not up to going out. は外出するだけの体力・気力がないという意味で、この to は不定詞標識ではなく前置詞なので going を用いる。The work is not up to standard. は仕事が必要水準に達していないことを表す。法律・広告などで上限を明確にする必要がある場合、up to だけでは最低値が示されないため、from X up to Y、up to and including Y などで範囲を明示することがある。
nuance.en: The meaning of up to changes substantially with context. Up to ten people means a maximum of ten and normally includes ten, but it does not promise that ten people will participate or establish any particular minimum. It’s up to you means that the choice or responsibility belongs to the listener. What are you up to? can neutrally ask what someone is doing or suspiciously ask what they are planning. I’m not up to going out means lacking sufficient energy, health, or willingness; to is a preposition here, so it is followed by the gerund going. The work is not up to standard means that it fails to reach the required level. In legal or promotional language, up to identifies a ceiling but not a floor, so from X up to Y or up to and including Y may be used when the full range requires clarification.

etymology.ja: up は古英語 up、upp「上へ」に由来し、to は古英語 tō「～へ、～まで」に由来する。物理的にある地点・高さへ向かい、その限界に到達するという組合せから、数量・時間・程度の「～まで」という意味が発達した。限界へ到達するという発想は be up to standard「基準まで達している」にも残る。責任・活動・能力を表す用法は、この空間的・限界的意味から比喩的に発達した。
etymology.en: Up derives from Old English up or upp, upward, while to comes from Old English tō, toward or as far as. Their combination originally indicated movement toward and arrival at a physical point or height. This spatial sense developed into the numerical, temporal, and scalar meaning as far as a particular limit. The image of reaching a level remains visible in be up to standard. The meanings involving responsibility, activity, and ability developed figuratively from these ideas of reaching, facing, or being equal to something.

grammar.transitivity: not applicable as an adjective phrase; tear is transitive or intransitive depending on sense
patterns: be torn between A and B
be torn between + noun and + noun
be torn between + gerund and + gerund
be torn between whether to do A or B, awkward

usage.between_pattern: The standard pattern for two competing alternatives is be torn between A and B.
usage.parallel_structure: The elements after between should normally have parallel forms: between staying and leaving.
usage.whether_pattern: For a full choice clause, use be torn over whether to do something or be unsure whether to do A or B.
usage.avoid_mixed_pattern: Be torn between whether ... is often awkward; use be torn between A and B or be torn over whether ... instead.
usage.emotion: The expression suggests that both alternatives exert a strong emotional or practical pull.
usage.predicative: Torn in this figurative sense is normally predicative: She was torn between the two offers.
usage.literal_sense: In a literal passive construction, be torn means be ripped or split: The document was torn.
usage.register: Natural in everyday, professional, and narrative English but less suitable than undecided or unable to determine in highly formal decisions.

ja: 二つ以上の選択肢の間で心が引き裂かれるように迷っている

en: to be deeply undecided between two or more alternatives
to feel strongly pulled by conflicting desires, duties, or emotions
to have difficulty deciding because each option has important advantages
to experience emotional conflict between competing loyalties, responsibilities, or values
literally, to be in a state of having been ripped or split

nuance.ja: be torn は、単に情報不足で決められないというより、複数の選択肢がそれぞれ強い魅力・義務・感情を伴い、心が別々の方向へ引かれている状態を表す。I’m torn between staying and leaving. なら、残る理由と去る理由の双方が強く、容易に決断できないという意味になる。undecided は結論が出ていないことを中立的に表すが、torn は内面的な葛藤を強調する。ambivalent は同じ対象について肯定的感情と否定的感情を同時に抱くことが中心で、必ずしも二つの選択肢から選ぶ場面とは限らない。on the fence は立場や選択を決めずにいる口語表現で、be torn ほど強い感情的葛藤を示さない場合がある。なお、The paper was torn. では比喩ではなく「紙が破れていた」という文字どおりの受動表現になる。
nuance.en: Be torn suggests more than lacking enough information to decide. It presents the alternatives as exerting strong emotional, practical, or moral pulls in different directions. I’m torn between staying and leaving means that compelling reasons support both choices and make the decision difficult. Undecided neutrally states that no decision has been reached, whereas torn emphasizes internal conflict. Ambivalent primarily describes simultaneous positive and negative feelings about the same person, object, or proposal and does not necessarily involve a choice between two alternatives. On the fence is an informal expression for withholding a decision or position and may imply less emotional conflict than be torn. In The paper was torn, however, the construction is literal and simply means that the paper had been ripped.

etymology.ja: torn は動詞 tear「引き裂く、破る」の過去分詞である。tear は古英語 teran「裂く、引き裂く」に由来し、ドイツ語 zehren などと歴史的に関係するゲルマン系の語である。物が二方向から引かれて裂けるという物理的なイメージから、人の心・忠誠・希望が相反する方向へ引かれる内面的葛藤を表す比喩が生じた。活用は tear–tore–torn であり、涙を意味する名詞 tear とは綴りが同じでも発音が異なる。
etymology.en: Torn is the past participle of tear, to rip or pull apart. Tear derives from Old English teran, to rend or tear, and belongs to a Germanic word family historically related to words including German zehren. The physical image of an object being pulled in opposing directions until it splits developed into a metaphor for a mind, loyalty, or desire pulled by incompatible alternatives. The verb forms are tear–tore–torn. The verb tear is pronounced differently from the identically spelled noun tear meaning a drop from the eye.

usage.contraction: It’ll is the contraction of it will and is especially common in speech and informal writing.
usage.future: Will presents the satisfactory outcome as a prediction or confident reassurance about the future.
usage.all_right: All right means satisfactory, safe, acceptable, or free from serious trouble in this expression.

usage.intonation: A calm falling intonation usually conveys confidence; uncertain or rising intonation can make the reassurance sound doubtful.
usage.it_reference: It may refer to a particular problem, the general situation, or an anticipated outcome.
usage.register: Natural in conversation; a formal context may require a more specific prediction or assessment.

en: the situation will probably have a satisfactory outcome

the feared result is unlikely to be as serious as expected
a reassurance meaning that there is no need to worry excessively

nuance.ja: It’ll be all right. は、不安や困難がある人に対して、状況は最終的に無事または満足できる形に落ち着くと伝える定型的な慰めの表現である。客観的な保証というより、話者の楽観・信頼・励ましを示す場合が多い。Don’t worry; it’ll be all right. は温かい励ましになり得る一方、深刻な問題に対して根拠なく使うと、相手の不安を軽視しているように響くこともある。Everything will be all right. は状況全体について、より包括的に安心させる。It’s all right. は現在の状態が問題ない、相手の行為を許す、または謝罪を受け入れる表現であり、未来の結果を予測する It’ll be all right. とは異なる。It’s going to be all right. は、状況が良い方向へ進んでいるという確信をやや強く感じさせることがある。
nuance.en: It’ll be all right is a conventional reassurance that a worrying or difficult situation will eventually reach a safe, manageable, or satisfactory outcome. It often expresses the speaker’s optimism, trust, or emotional support rather than an objective guarantee. Don’t worry; it’ll be all right can be warm and comforting, but if used without grounds in response to a serious problem, it may sound as though the speaker is dismissing the other person’s concerns. Everything will be all right offers broader reassurance about the entire situation. It’s all right refers to a present condition, grants permission, or accepts an apology, whereas It’ll be all right predicts a future outcome. It’s going to be all right may sometimes suggest slightly stronger confidence based on how the situation appears to be developing.

en: It’ll be all right reassures someone that the future outcome will be safe, manageable, or satisfactory.

Everything will be all right gives broader reassurance concerning the whole situation.
It’ll be okay is a very common conversational near-equivalent of It’ll be all right.

You’ll be all right reassures the listener about their own health, safety, or condition.
It should be all right predicts an acceptable outcome while leaving some uncertainty.
Things will work out reassures someone that problems will eventually be resolved satisfactorily.

etymology.ja: It’ll は it will の短縮形で、will は古英語 willan「望む、意図する」に由来し、後に未来・予測を表す助動詞となった。right は古英語 riht「正しい、まっすぐな、公正な」に由来する。all right は文字どおりには「すべて正しい状態」を表し、そこから「問題がない、満足できる、無事である」という意味を発達させた。It will be all right. は、この状態が将来実現するという予測から、安心や励ましを与える定型表現となった。
etymology.en: It’ll is the contraction of it will. Will derives from Old English willan, to wish or intend, and later developed its auxiliary use for futurity and prediction. Right comes from Old English riht, correct, straight, or just. All right literally suggested that everything was in a correct condition and developed the senses satisfactory, free from trouble, and safe. It will be all right consequently became a conventional prediction used to provide comfort and reassurance.

en: an expression meaning that something has been needlessly lost or used badly
an expression of disappointment about wasted time, money, food, or another resource
regret that an opportunity, ability, or useful object was not properly used
a critical reaction to unnecessary loss or inefficiency
dissatisfaction that an expected object, event, or activity proved useless

nuance.ja: What a waste! は、価値のある物・時間・金銭・機会・能力などが役立てられず失われたことへの残念さや批判を表す。食べ物が捨てられた場面なら「もったいない」、不要な会議なら「まったく時間の無駄だ」、才能が生かされていない場面なら「才能がもったいない」に相当する。What a shame! や What a pity! は残念な出来事全般に使えるが、What a waste! は本来なら有効に使えた価値・可能性が失われたことに焦点を置く。人について He’s a waste. や What a waste. と直接言うと、その人自身に価値がないと評価するような非常に侮辱的な響きになり得る。What a waste of talent. とすれば、批判の対象を人そのものではなく、活用されていない能力へ向けられる。
nuance.en: What a waste expresses regret or criticism because something valuable—such as time, money, food, opportunity, or ability—has been lost or used badly. When food is discarded, it corresponds to the idea that the food should not have been wasted. Applied to an unnecessary meeting, it may mean a complete waste of time. Applied to unused ability, it means that valuable talent has not been developed or employed. What a shame and What a pity can respond to unfortunate events generally, whereas What a waste focuses on value or potential that could have been used productively. Directly calling a person a waste can be severely insulting because it may deny the person’s own worth. What a waste of talent instead directs criticism toward the failure to use the ability.

etymology.ja: waste は古フランス語 wast、vast「荒れた、空虚な」に由来し、ラテン語 vastus「荒れ果てた、広大で空の」と関係する。もとは土地が人に利用されず荒廃している状態を表し、そこから資源・時間・能力などが有効に使われず失われる意味へ発達した。What a ...! は驚き・感嘆・非難を表す英語の感嘆構文であり、What a waste! は「これは何という無駄なのか」という形から、強い残念さを示す定型表現となった。
etymology.en: Waste came through Old French wast or vast, desolate or empty, and is related to Latin vastus, desolate, immense, or empty. It originally described land left uninhabited or uncultivated and developed the meaning of failing to use resources, time, or ability productively. What a ...! is an English exclamative construction expressing surprise, admiration, or criticism. What a waste therefore developed from the literal idea what an instance of waste this is into a fixed reaction of strong regret or disappointment.

grammar.transitivity: transitive when meaning annoy or pressure someone; intransitive when meaning argue or dispute

usage.countable: A hassle means an inconvenient, annoying, or troublesome situation: Getting a refund was a hassle.
usage.uncountable: Hassle can be uncountable when referring generally to inconvenience or difficulty: without hassle.
usage.verb_person: To hassle someone means repeatedly annoy, pressure, question, or cause difficulty for that person.
usage.argument: Used intransitively, hassle can mean argue or dispute, especially over a minor matter.
usage.of_pattern: The hassle of is followed by a noun or gerund: the hassle of changing trains.
usage.severity: Hassle usually describes irritating inconvenience rather than a severe danger or disaster.
usage.harass_contrast: Hassle is informal and often less severe than harass, although repeated hassling can amount to harassment depending on the conduct.
usage.register: Highly natural in informal conversation; inconvenience, difficulty, administrative burden, or harass may be more suitable in formal writing.

en: an inconvenient or troublesome situation requiring unnecessary time or effort
annoyance or difficulty associated with a procedure, journey, purchase, or negotiation
a minor argument, dispute, or conflict
as a verb, to repeatedly annoy, question, or cause difficulty for someone
to pressure someone into doing something they may not wish to do
to argue or dispute with someone over a relatively minor matter

nuance.ja: hassle は、重大な危機というより、余計な手間・待ち時間・交渉・書類作業などによって感じる「面倒くささ」を口語的に表す。Filling out the forms was a hassle. は、書類作成が不可能だったのではなく、煩雑で時間や労力を奪われたという意味である。trouble は問題・困難をより広く表し、inconvenience は丁寧で中立的、nuisance は迷惑を生じさせる人・物・状況に焦点を置く。動詞 hassle は Don’t hassle me. のように、人へ繰り返しうるさく言ったり圧力をかけたりすることを表し、名詞より批判的になりやすい。harass は反復的・深刻・違法になり得る嫌がらせにも使われる、より強く形式的な語であるため、通常の小さな面倒には hassle の方が自然である。
nuance.en: Hassle informally describes inconvenience caused by extra effort, delay, negotiation, paperwork, or minor conflict rather than a major crisis. Filling out the forms was a hassle means that the task was burdensome and time-consuming, not necessarily impossible. Trouble is broader and can describe difficulties of any severity. Inconvenience is more neutral and polite, while nuisance focuses on a person, thing, or situation that repeatedly causes annoyance. As a verb, hassle is more directly critical: Don’t hassle me asks someone to stop repeatedly questioning, pressuring, or bothering the speaker. Harass is a stronger and more formal word that can describe persistent, severe, or legally actionable mistreatment; hassle is more natural for ordinary irritating pressure or inconvenience.

ja: hassle：余計な時間・労力を要する面倒、または人にうるさく圧力をかけること。
trouble：問題・困難・心配・不都合を広く表す一般語。

en: a hassle is an irritating inconvenience requiring extra effort, while the verb means repeatedly bothering or pressuring someone.
trouble is the broad general term for a problem, difficulty, worry, or inconvenience.
inconvenience is a more neutral and polite term for disruption to comfort or plans.
bother is an everyday word for annoying someone or making an unnecessary effort.
a nuisance is a person, thing, or situation that repeatedly causes annoyance or inconvenience.
an annoyance is an irritating event or the feeling of being irritated.
harass means subjecting someone to persistent or aggressive mistreatment and is stronger and more formal than hassle.
fuss is excessive worry, complaint, or activity concerning something relatively unimportant.

etymology.ja: hassle は20世紀半ばにアメリカ英語で広まった比較的新しい語で、正確な起源は確定していない。haggle「値段などをめぐって言い争う」と tussle「もみ合う、争う」の影響を受けた混成語である可能性がしばしば指摘される。当初は口論・もめ事・人を困らせることを表し、そこから手続きや作業に伴う「面倒、煩わしさ」という現在の一般的な名詞用法が発達した。
etymology.en: Hassle is a relatively recent word that became widespread in mid-twentieth-century American English. Its exact origin is uncertain. It is often suggested that the word was influenced by, or formed as a blend of, haggle, to argue over terms or price, and tussle, to struggle or fight. Its earlier uses involved disputes, arguments, and bothering another person. From these developed the now common noun sense of an inconvenient, troublesome, or unnecessarily demanding process.

nuance.ja: budget は、単なる資金額ではなく、一定期間または特定事業について、利用可能な金銭をどのように配分するかを示す計画である。a budget of $10,000 は総額1万ドルの予算、a budget for advertising は広告用の予算を意味する。within budget は予定額を超えずに、under budget は予定額より少ない費用で、over budget は予算超過で、という意味になる。on a tight budget は使える金銭が限られている状態を表す。estimate は特定の費用についての予測額、forecast は将来の収入・支出・経済状態などの予測であり、必ずしも支出権限や上限を設定しない。形容詞的な budget は budget airline や budget hotel のように、低価格を優先し、サービスを簡素化した商品・事業を表す。
nuance.en: A budget is not merely an amount of money but a plan for allocating available funds over a period or to a particular activity. A budget of $10,000 states the total amount, while a budget for advertising identifies its purpose. Within budget means without exceeding the planned amount, under budget means at a lower cost than planned, and over budget means beyond the approved or expected amount. On a tight budget indicates that only limited funds are available. An estimate predicts the likely cost of a particular item or job, while a forecast predicts future income, expenditure, or economic conditions and does not necessarily authorize spending or establish a ceiling. Attributive budget, as in budget airline or budget hotel, describes a low-priced offering that commonly provides simpler or more limited services.

etymology.ja: 古フランス語 bougette「小さな革袋」に由来する。bougette は bouge「革袋、財布」の指小形で、さらにラテン語 bulga「革袋」にさかのぼる。イギリスでは、財務大臣が政府の財政計画を記した書類を袋に入れて議会へ持参したことから、その袋を開いて財政案を提示することが the budget と呼ばれるようになった。そこから、政府だけでなく企業・家庭・個人の収支計画や利用可能な資金額を広く表すようになった。
etymology.en: Budget derives from Old French bougette, a small leather bag, the diminutive of bouge, a leather bag or wallet, ultimately from Latin bulga, a leather bag. In Britain, the Chancellor of the Exchequer traditionally brought financial proposals to Parliament in a bag, and opening or presenting the budget came to refer to presenting the government’s financial plan. The word consequently shifted from the container to its fiscal contents and later broadened to cover the income-and-expenditure plans of businesses, households, projects, and individuals.

usage.spacing: Extra budget is written as two words. Extrabudget as a single ordinary word is nonstandard or highly exceptional.
usage.meaning: An extra budget is an additional government spending and revenue plan adopted after or in addition to the main annual budget.
usage.formal_term: Supplementary budget is generally the clearer and more established formal term.
usage.purpose: It may address an emergency, unexpected expenditure, changed economic conditions, or a new government policy.

nuance.ja: extra budget は、日本語の「補正予算」を説明する際に報道などで使われることがあるが、正式かつ国際的に分かりやすい表現としては supplementary budget の方が安定している。extra budget は、当初の年間予算に含まれていなかった緊急支出・景気対策・物価高対策などを追加する予算を指す。単に各部門へ追加で与えられる予算なら additional budget や additional funding の方が自然な場合もある。extrabudgetary または extra-budgetary は「正規の予算制度・予算書の外にある」という別の概念であり、extrabudgetary fund は必ずしも補正予算によって設けられた基金ではない。したがって、extrabudget を一語の名詞として登録するより、extra budget を見出し語とし、supplementary budget を標準的な言い換えとして覚えるのが安全である。
nuance.en: Extra budget occurs in journalism and in explanations of an additional government budget, including translations of the Japanese concept of a supplementary budget. Supplementary budget is nevertheless the more stable and internationally transparent formal expression. An extra budget commonly provides for emergency expenditure, economic support, cost-of-living measures, or another need not adequately covered by the original annual budget. If the subject is merely additional money assigned to a department or project, additional budget or additional funding may be more natural. Extrabudgetary or extra-budgetary has a different meaning: it describes funds or operations outside the regular budgetary framework. An extrabudgetary fund is therefore not necessarily a fund created through a supplementary budget. It is safer to record extra budget as two words and learn supplementary budget as its principal formal equivalent.

Extra budget is therefore a transparent two-word expression meaning a budget additional to the ordinary or original one. Extrabudgetary, by contrast, combines extra- with budgetary and means existing outside the regular budgetary system.

usage.transitive: Used transitively, loosen means make something less tight, firm, restrictive, or controlled.
usage.intransitive: Used intransitively, it means become less tight or firmly fixed: The knot loosened.
usage.physical: It commonly applies to knots, screws, lids, clothing, soil, muscles, and a person’s grip.
usage.rules: Figuratively, loosen restrictions or controls means make them less strict.
usage.policy: Loosen monetary policy means make financial conditions more accommodative, although ease monetary policy is often more idiomatic.
usage.loosen_up: Loosen up can mean become physically relaxed, behave less formally, or prepare muscles for activity.
usage.loose_lose_warning: Loosen is derived from loose and contains the /s/ sound; it must not be confused with lose, pronounced with /z/.
usage.tighten_opposite: Tighten is the direct opposite in both physical and many figurative uses.

en: to make a knot, screw, lid, garment, or fastening less tight

nuance.ja: loosen は、物理的・比喩的に「締まりや拘束の程度を弱める」ことを表す。loosen a screw はねじを完全に取り外すのではなく、締め付けを弱くすること、loosen one’s tie はネクタイを外さず緩めることを意味する。規制について loosen restrictions と言えば、規制を廃止するのではなく、適用条件や厳しさを緩和する。relax restrictions もほぼ同じだが、loosen は締め付けを弱めるという比喩がより明確である。ease は痛み・負担・緊張・政策などを徐々に軽減することに重点を置く。loosen up は、筋肉をほぐすほか、人が緊張を解いてくだけた態度になることも表す。なお、loose は「緩い」、lose は「失う」で、綴りと発音の双方が異なる。
nuance.en: Loosen means reducing tightness or restraint, either physically or figuratively. Loosen a screw means reducing its tightness rather than necessarily removing it, while loosen one’s tie means making it less tight without taking it off. Loosen restrictions means reducing their strictness or narrowing their constraints, not abolishing them altogether. Relax restrictions is very close, but loosen more clearly preserves the metaphor of reducing a tight grip. Ease focuses on gradually reducing pain, burden, tension, or restrictive policy. Loosen up can describe relaxing muscles or becoming less tense, formal, or inhibited. Loose means not tight, whereas lose means cease to possess; the two words differ in both spelling and pronunciation.

etymology.ja: 形容詞 loose に、「～にする、～になる」を表す動詞接尾辞 -en が付いて成立した。loose は古ノルド語 lauss「自由な、結び付けられていない」に由来し、古英語 lēas とも関係するゲルマン系の語である。もともとは束縛・固定から解放された状態を表し、loosen は「固定や締付けを弱め、そのような状態にする」という意味になった。そこから、規則・支配・金融政策などの厳しさを弱める比喩的用法も発達した。
etymology.en: Loosen was formed from the adjective loose with the verb-forming suffix -en, meaning make or become. Loose derives from Old Norse lauss, free or unattached, and is related to Old English lēas within the Germanic language family. Its underlying sense was freedom from binding or secure attachment. Loosen therefore came to mean making something less firmly bound or fixed. This physical meaning subsequently extended to reducing the strictness of rules, control, restrictions, and economic policy.

nuance.ja: slacken は、張力・速度・勢い・努力などが、それまでの強さを失って緩むことを表す。物理的には slacken the rope のように、張っているロープを少し緩めることを意味する。比喩的には demand slackened「需要が弱まった」、the pace slackened「ペースが落ちた」、slacken one’s efforts「努力を緩める」のように使う。loosen と重なるが、loosen は結び目・衣服・規則などを広く「緩くする」語であり、slacken は特に張力、勢い、速度、活動の程度が低下する過程に焦点を置く。経済については weaken や slow よりやや形式的で、緩やかな減速を表すことが多い。
nuance.en: Slacken describes a loss of tension, speed, force, or effort from a previously stronger state. Physically, slacken the rope means reducing the tension in a taut rope. Figuratively, demand slackened indicates weakening demand, the pace slackened indicates a reduction in speed, and slacken one’s efforts means applying less energy or determination. It overlaps with loosen, but loosen broadly applies to knots, clothing, restrictions, and other things made less tight or restrictive. Slacken focuses more particularly on declining tension, momentum, speed, or activity. In economic writing it is somewhat formal and often suggests a gradual slowing rather than a sudden collapse.

etymology.en: Slacken was formed from the adjective slack with the verb-forming suffix -en. Slack comes from Old English slæc, which carried meanings such as loose, inactive, negligent, or slow. The physical idea of lacking tension was extended to reductions in speed, demand, effort, discipline, and intensity. The formation is comparable to verbs such as strengthen and weaken.

to remove or bring an end to a nuisance, obstruction, or unlawful condition

nuance.ja: abate は、強く続いていた不快・有害な現象が弱まること、またはそれを弱めることを表す形式的な語である。The storm abated. なら嵐の勢いが収まり、Her anger abated. なら怒りが徐々に和らいだことを意味する。目的語を取る場合は、pollution、risk、nuisance など、抑制または除去すべき好ましくない対象と結び付きやすい。slacken は速度・努力・需要・張力などが緩むことに焦点を置くのに対し、abate は苦痛、悪天候、危険、騒動などの深刻さ・強度が低下することを強調する。法律用語としての abate a nuisance は、単に迷惑の程度を軽くするだけでなく、その状態を停止・除去することまで含み得る。
nuance.en: Abate is a formal verb describing the weakening of a persistent unpleasant or harmful condition, or action taken to reduce it. The storm abated means that the storm lost intensity, while her anger abated indicates that the emotion gradually subsided. In transitive use, it commonly takes an undesirable object such as pollution, risk, or a nuisance that is to be controlled or removed. Slacken focuses more readily on reductions in speed, effort, demand, or tension, whereas abate emphasizes diminished severity or intensity in pain, bad weather, danger, or disturbance. In legal language, to abate a nuisance may involve terminating or removing the condition rather than merely making it less serious.

etymology.ja: abate は古フランス語 abatre「打ち倒す、低くする、弱める」を経て英語に入った。この語は a-「～へ」と battre「打つ」から成り、battre はラテン語 battuere「打つ、たたく」にさかのぼる。もともとの「打ち倒す、低くする」という物理的な意味から、力・勢い・苦痛・価格などを減少させる意味が発達した。名詞 abatement は「減少・軽減」のほか、法律・税務・環境分野で「除去・排除・減免」などを表す。
etymology.en: Abate entered English through Old French abatre, meaning to strike down, lower, or weaken. The French word was formed from a- and battre, to beat, which ultimately derives from Latin battuere, to beat or strike. The physical idea of striking something down or bringing it lower developed into the senses of reducing force, intensity, pain, or price. The related noun abatement can mean reduction or relief and has specialized uses involving removal, suppression, or remission in legal, tax, and environmental contexts.

usage.legal_scope: The availability and precise effect of an abatement depend on the relevant jurisdiction, statute, contract, or administrative scheme.

nuance.ja: abatement は、好ましくない現象の強度・量・影響を弱めることを表す、主に形式的・専門的な名詞である。pollution abatement や noise abatement では、単なる自然な減少ではなく、設備・規制・対策による積極的な抑制を指すことが多い。nuisance abatement は、法律上の迷惑状態を軽減するだけでなく、その原因を停止・除去することまで含み得る。tax abatement や rent abatement では、一定の条件に基づく税金・賃料の減額または免除を意味する。reduction より専門性が高く、alleviation が苦痛・困難の緩和に焦点を置くのに対し、abatement は測定可能な排出量、法的な迷惑状態、金銭債務などにも広く用いられる。
nuance.en: Abatement is a mainly formal or technical noun for reducing the intensity, amount, or harmful effect of an undesirable condition. In pollution abatement and noise abatement, it often refers to active control through equipment, regulation, or other measures rather than a merely natural decline. Nuisance abatement may require the source of a legally recognized nuisance to be stopped or removed, not simply made less serious. Tax abatement and rent abatement refer to a reduction, exemption, or suspension granted under specified conditions. The word is more specialized than reduction. Whereas alleviation focuses particularly on relieving suffering or difficulty, abatement also applies readily to measurable emissions, legal nuisances, and financial liabilities.

etymology.ja: abatement は動詞 abate に、行為・過程・結果を表す接尾辞 -ment が付いて成立した。abate は古フランス語 abatre「打ち倒す、低くする、弱める」に由来し、その battre「打つ」はラテン語 battuere にさかのぼる。したがって原義には、何かを打ち倒して低い状態にするというイメージがある。そこから、勢い・量・価格・負担を減少させることや、迷惑状態を除去することを表す専門的な意味が発達した。
etymology.en: Abatement was formed from the verb abate with the noun-forming suffix -ment, denoting an act, process, or result. Abate came from Old French abatre, meaning to strike down, lower, or weaken; its element battre, to beat, ultimately derives from Latin battuere. The original image was therefore that of bringing something down. From this developed the specialized senses of reducing force, quantity, price, or burden and removing a nuisance or harmful condition.

nuance.en: Although contractant transparently means one who contracts, it is exceedingly uncommon in contemporary standard legal English. etymology.en: Contractant was borrowed from French contractant, a person or party entering into a contract, originally the present participle of contracter, to contract. nuance.en: Contracting party is the standard legal expression for an entity that has entered into a contract and holds rights or assumes obligations under it. A third party is outside the contract, and a third-party beneficiary does not become a contracting party merely because the contract benefits that person. In treaties and international registration systems, capitalized Contracting Party may instead designate a participating state or intergovernmental organization.

nuance.ja: counterparty は、ある当事者を基準にして、その契約・取引の「反対側にいる相手」を表す相対的な語である。A社とB社が取引する場合、A社から見ればB社が counterparty であり、B社から見ればA社が counterparty となる。contracting party は契約当事者であるという客観的な地位に焦点を置くが、counterparty は特定の当事者から見た相手方という関係に焦点を置く。金融分野で特によく使われ、counterparty risk は相手方が支払・引渡し・決済などの義務を履行しない危険をいう。契約当事者が三者以上いる場合には、other party、relevant party、名称で定義した当事者などを使う方が、どの相手を指すか明確な場合がある。
nuance.en: Counterparty is a relational term for the participant on the other side of a contract or transaction from the perspective of a particular party. If Company A trades with Company B, B is A’s counterparty and A is B’s counterparty. Contracting party emphasizes the objective status of having entered into the contract, whereas counterparty emphasizes the relationship between one participant and the other side. The word is especially common in finance, where counterparty risk concerns the possibility that the other party will fail to make payment, deliver an asset, settle the transaction, or perform another obligation. In an agreement involving more than two parties, other party, relevant party, or a specifically defined party name may identify the intended entity more clearly.

Counter- derives from Latin contra, against or opposite, while party entered English through Old French partie and is related to Latin partire, to divide. The word therefore literally identifies the party on the opposite side of a transaction. It became especially prominent in late twentieth-century financial regulation and risk management through expressions such as counterparty risk and counterparty exposure.

nuance.ja: de facto の核心は、名目・法的形式・公式な承認ではなく、現実に存在する状態や機能に注目することである。a de facto leader は正式な役職に就いていなくても実際に組織を指揮する人物、a de facto standard は公的機関が制定した規格でなくても市場で広く採用されている標準をいう。反対語の de jure は「法律上・正式には」を意味する。ただし、de facto が直ちに「違法」「無効」「不当」を意味するわけではない。事実上の状態が法律上も一定の効果を認められる場合もあれば、法的地位をまったく持たない場合もある。したがって、法律文書では、単なる実態の説明なのか、そこから何らかの法的効果を主張するのかを明確にする必要がある。
nuance.en: The core of de facto is attention to actual conditions or functions rather than formal title, legal form, or official recognition. A de facto leader directs an organization in practice without necessarily holding the formal office. A de facto standard is widely followed in the market even though it may not have been formally adopted by an official standards body. Its opposite, de jure, means existing by law or formal right. De facto does not automatically mean illegal, invalid, or improper. A factual arrangement may receive some legal recognition in a particular context, or it may possess no formal legal status at all. Legal writing should therefore clarify whether the phrase merely describes reality or is also being used to support a claimed legal consequence.

etymology.ja: de facto はラテン語の句で、de「～から、～に基づいて」と factum「行われたこと、事実」から成り、文字どおりには「事実に基づいて」を意味する。factum は facere「作る、行う」の過去分詞に由来し、英語の fact と同語源である。法律上の権利・形式を表す de jure「法に基づいて」と対比され、政治・法律・外交などの分野から一般の英語へ広がった。
etymology.en: De facto is a Latin phrase formed from de, from or on the basis of, and facto, the ablative form of factum, a deed or fact. Factum derives from the past participle of facere, to make or do, and is also the source of English fact. The phrase became established in contrast with de jure, on the basis of law, particularly in legal, political, and diplomatic language before spreading into general English.

nuance.ja: de jure は、現実に何が行われているかではなく、法律・規則・正式な権限によって認められている状態を表す。a de jure leader は法律上または正式には指導者である人物を指すが、実権を別の人物が握っている可能性がある。反対に de facto leader は正式な地位がなくても実際に指揮している人物である。ただし、de jure と de facto は常に対立するわけではなく、一人の人物が法律上も事実上も指導者である場合もある。また、de jure は単に「合法的な」という評価語ではなく、特定の権限・地位・制度が法的に成立していることを示す。法律文書では、形式上の権利と実際の支配・運用のどちらを論じているかを明確にする必要がある。
nuance.en: De jure describes a status recognized by law, rule, or formal authority rather than what happens in actual practice. A de jure leader holds the office legally or officially, although another person may exercise the real power. Conversely, a de facto leader exercises authority in practice without necessarily holding the formal position. De jure and de facto are not always opposed: the same person or arrangement may possess both formal legal status and practical reality. De jure is not merely an evaluative synonym for lawful; it indicates that a particular status, authority, right, or system exists as a matter of law. Legal writing should make clear whether it concerns formal entitlement or actual control and operation.

usage.adjective: Before a noun, in vitro describes testing, research, or a process conducted outside a living organism in a laboratory setting.
usage.adverb: As an adverb, it means outside a living organism or in laboratory conditions: The cells were cultured in vitro.
usage.scope: The term is not limited to literal glass vessels and may include plastic culture dishes, microplates, and other laboratory systems.
usage.diagnostics: In vitro diagnostics are tests performed on specimens such as blood or tissue taken from the human body.
usage.fertilization: In vitro fertilization involves combining eggs and sperm outside the body to create embryos before subsequent transfer or preservation.
usage.contrast: In vivo refers to a process or experiment occurring within a living organism.
usage.hyphenation: The established scientific expression is generally written in vitro without a hyphen, including before a noun, although some editorial styles use in-vitro.
usage.italics: Scientific style guides differ on italics; consistent treatment within a document is advisable.

as an adjective, relating to laboratory processes conducted outside a living organism

nuance.ja: in vitro は「試験管内で」と訳されることが多いが、実際には試験管やガラス容器に限定されず、培養皿・マイクロプレート・人工膜などを用いる生体外の実験系を広く含む。in vitro experiment は条件を制御しやすく、細胞や分子に対する直接的な作用を調べるのに適している一方、代謝・免疫・臓器間相互作用などを含む生体全体の反応を完全には再現できないことがある。そのため、ある物質が in vitro で効果を示しても、人間または動物の体内で同じ効果を示すとは限らない。in vivo は生体内、ex vivo は生体から取り出した組織・臓器などを比較的本来の状態を保ちながら調べる実験を指すことが多いが、in vitro と ex vivo の境界は分野によって必ずしも一貫しない。
nuance.en: In vitro is often translated literally as in a test tube, but it is not restricted to test tubes or glass vessels. It broadly includes experimental systems outside a living organism, such as culture dishes, microplates, and artificial membranes. In vitro experiments permit close control of conditions and are useful for examining direct effects on cells or molecules, but they may not reproduce whole-organism processes such as metabolism, immunity, and interactions among organs. Consequently, an effect demonstrated in vitro does not necessarily occur in a human or animal body. In vivo means within a living organism. Ex vivo commonly concerns tissues or organs removed from an organism and studied while retaining aspects of their original state, although the boundary between ex vivo and in vitro is not entirely consistent across disciplines.

etymology.ja: in vitro はラテン語で、in「～の中で」と vitro「ガラス」によって構成され、文字どおりには「ガラスの中で」を意味する。vitro は vitrum「ガラス」の奪格形であり、英語の vitreous「ガラス質の」や vitrify「ガラス化する」と同語族である。初期の生物学的実験でガラス製の試験管・培養容器が使われたことから、生体外の実験環境を表す語として定着した。現代では容器がプラスチックなどであっても in vitro と呼ばれる。
etymology.en: In vitro is Latin for in glass, formed from in and vitro, the ablative form of vitrum, glass. Vitrum is also related to English words such as vitreous and vitrify. Because early biological experiments outside the body were conducted in glass test tubes and culture vessels, the phrase became established for laboratory work outside a living organism. In modern usage, a process may be described as in vitro even when the vessel is made of plastic or another material.

note.en: Describes testing based on cultured cells, although not every in vitro system contains living cells.

note.en: A broader adjective describing work based on laboratory facilities or methods.

A patent application claiming an in vitro assay should describe the experimental conditions sufficiently clearly to support the claimed invention. — 生体外アッセイを請求する特許出願では、請求された発明を裏付けられる程度に実験条件を明確に記載すべきである。

The compound inhibited viral replication in vitro.

usage.adjective: Before a noun, in vivo describes research, testing, or a process occurring within a living organism.
usage.adverb: As an adverb, it means within a living organism: The compound was tested in vivo.
usage.subjects: Depending on context, the living organism may be a human, animal, plant, microorganism, or another living system.
usage.research: In biomedical research, in vivo studies allow effects to be observed in the context of metabolism, circulation, immunity, and interactions among organs.
usage.contrast: In vitro refers to work outside a living organism in a laboratory system.
usage.human_studies: In vivo does not automatically mean a human clinical study; many in vivo experiments are conducted using animal models.
usage.hyphenation: The established expression is normally written in vivo without a hyphen, including before a noun.
usage.italics: It need not be italicized in ordinary scientific English, although editorial styles vary.

under conditions in which the interactions of cells, tissues, and organs remain present
for a substance, tested by administration to or observation within a living organism
relating to an effect, reaction, or metabolic process occurring inside a living body
as an adjective, involving or conducted within a living organism

nuance.ja: in vivo は、生きている生物の体内で現象を観察・測定することを表す。in vitro 実験では細胞や分子への直接的な作用を制御された条件下で調べられるが、in vivo 実験では吸収・分布・代謝・排泄、免疫反応、臓器間相互作用などを含む生体全体での効果を評価できる。その反面、個体差や多数の生物学的要因が関与するため、結果の解釈は複雑になりやすい。また、in vivo study は人を対象とする臨床試験に限られず、動物モデルを用いる実験も含む。in vitro で確認された効果が in vivo で再現されるとは限らず、in vivo で効果が示されても、人への有効性や安全性が直ちに証明されるわけではない。
nuance.en: In vivo describes observation or measurement within a living organism. An in vitro experiment can examine direct effects on cells or molecules under controlled conditions, whereas an in vivo study can evaluate effects in the context of absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, immune responses, and interactions among organs. The involvement of numerous biological factors and individual variation can, however, make in vivo results more complex to interpret. An in vivo study is not necessarily a human clinical trial; it may use an animal model. An effect found in vitro may not be reproduced in vivo, and efficacy in an animal in vivo model does not by itself establish efficacy or safety in humans.

ja: in vivo：生きている人・動物などの生体内で。
in vitro：細胞・組織・検体などを、生体外の実験室環境で扱って。
ex vivo：生体から取り出した組織・臓器などを、本来の状態に近い形で生体外において。
in situ：対象を取り出さず、本来存在する位置・場所において。
in silico：コンピューターによるモデル・シミュレーションを用いて。
preclinical：人を対象とする臨床試験に先立つ研究段階の。
clinical：患者・人の健康管理または人を対象とする研究に関する。
animal model：人の疾患・生理現象などを研究するために用いる動物または実験系。

in vitro means outside a living organism in a controlled laboratory environment.
ex vivo commonly means outside the body using tissue or an organ removed while retaining aspects of its original state.
in situ means in the original place or position without removing the subject.
in silico means using a computer model or simulation.
preclinical describes research conducted before testing a treatment in human clinical trials.
clinical relates to patients, medical care, or research involving human participants.
an animal model is an animal or experimental system used to investigate human physiology, disease, or treatment.

etymology.ja: in vivo はラテン語の句で、in「～の中で」と vivo「生きているもの」によって構成され、文字どおりには「生きているものの中で」を意味する。vivo は vivus「生きている」の奪格形であり、英語の vivid、revive、survive、vital などと同じく、生命を表す印欧語根に関係する。生体外の人工的環境を表す in vitro との対比により、医学・生物学・薬理学で広く用いられるようになった。
etymology.en: In vivo is a Latin phrase formed from in and vivo, the ablative form of vivus, living or alive. It therefore literally means within the living. Vivus is related to a wider Indo-European family concerning life, reflected in English words such as vivid, revive, survive, and vital. The phrase became widely established in medicine, biology, and pharmacology in contrast with in vitro, outside a living organism.

note.ja: in vivo の意味を専門用語を避けて直接説明する表現。
note.en: A direct plain-language explanation of in vivo that avoids the Latin scientific term.

note.ja: 人体・動物体内で生じることを平易に表すが、植物などには適さない場合がある。
note.en: A plain expression for something occurring within a human or animal body, though less suitable for plants.

note.ja: 単離した細胞・組織ではなく、生物個体全体を対象とすることを強調する。
note.en: Emphasizes that an entire organism rather than isolated cells or tissues is being studied.

note.ja: 動物を使用する研究を表すが、in vivo は人・植物なども対象にできるため完全な同義語ではない。
note.en: Describes research using animals, but is not fully synonymous because in vivo can also concern humans or plants.

note.ja: 生物の正常な機能・過程に関する語であり、生体内で行うという実験場所そのものを必ずしも示さない。
note.en: Relates to the functions and processes of living organisms but does not necessarily specify an in vivo experimental setting.

grammar.countability: countable as a legal agreement; used without an article in expressions such as under contract
grammar.transitivity: transitive or intransitive as a verb, depending on meaning
patterns: enter into / sign / perform a contract

usage.noun: A contract is an agreement creating legally enforceable rights or obligations, subject to the requirements of the applicable law.
usage.document: Contract may refer either to the legal agreement itself or to the document recording its terms.
usage.oral_contract: A contract is not necessarily written or signed; oral and conduct-based contracts may be enforceable, although some contracts must satisfy formal requirements.
usage.agreement_distinction: Agreement is broader than contract because not every agreement is intended or legally able to create enforceable obligations.
usage.contracting_verb: To contract with someone means to enter into a legally binding agreement with that person or organization.
usage.commission_verb: To contract someone to do work means to formally engage that person or business to perform it.
usage.shrink_verb: When a muscle, material, or volume contracts, it becomes shorter, tighter, or smaller.
usage.disease_verb: To contract a disease or infection means to become infected with or develop it.
usage.pronunciation: The noun is stressed on the first syllable, while the verb is normally stressed on the second syllable.

a written document recording the terms of a legal agreement
to enter into a contract with a person or organization
to formally engage a person or company to perform work
to become infected with or develop a disease

for a material or volume, to become smaller
to incur a debt, obligation, or liability

nuance.ja: 名詞の contract は、単なる約束や了解ではなく、原則として法的拘束力を持つ合意を表す。ただし、成立要件、約因の必要性、書面・署名の要否などは法域と契約類型によって異なる。契約書という紙や電子文書を指すこともあるが、契約そのものと契約を証する文書は概念上同一とは限らない。動詞 contract は「契約する」のほか、contract a disease「病気にかかる」、muscles contract「筋肉が収縮する」の意味を持つ。名詞では第一音節、動詞では第二音節に強勢を置く。日本語の「委託する」に当たる意味で人を目的語にする場合、contract someone to do の形は使えるが、日常的には hire や commission の方が自然な場合もある。
nuance.en: As a noun, contract normally denotes an agreement intended and legally capable of creating enforceable rights or obligations rather than a merely social promise or informal understanding. Requirements concerning formation, consideration, writing, and signature vary by jurisdiction and type of transaction. Contract may also refer to the paper or electronic document recording the agreement, although the legal relationship and the document evidencing it are conceptually distinct. As a verb, contract also means acquire a disease or become physically smaller or tighter. The noun carries first-syllable stress, whereas the verb carries second-syllable stress. Contract someone to do something is possible for formally engaging a service provider, although hire or commission may be more natural in everyday contexts.

ja: contract：法的に強制可能な権利・義務を生じさせる契約、または契約する。
agreement：二者以上の合意を広く表し、必ずしも法的拘束力を持たない。
arrangement：当事者間で決めた実務上の取り決め。形式性・法的拘束力は文脈による。

en: a contract is a legally enforceable agreement, or contract means entering such an agreement.
an agreement broadly means a shared understanding and is not necessarily legally enforceable.
an arrangement is a practical understanding whose formality and legal force depend on context.
a covenant is a solemn or formal promise, often contained in a contract or deed.
an undertaking is a formal promise to perform or refrain from a particular act.
hire means employing someone or paying to use property or services for a period.
contract also means becoming physically shorter, tighter, or smaller.

etymology.ja: contract はラテン語 contractus に由来し、これは contrahere「引き合わせる、集める、縮める、契約する」の過去分詞である。contrahere は con-「共に」と trahere「引く」から成る。「物を引き合わせる」という発想から、当事者を合意によって結び付ける「契約」の意味と、物理的に引き締める「収縮」の意味が発達した。病気にかかる意味は、病気や感染を自らの身に引き受けるという用法から生じた。
etymology.en: Contract derives from Latin contractus, the past participle of contrahere, meaning to draw together, collect, shorten, or make an agreement. Contrahere was formed from con-, together, and trahere, to draw. The idea of drawing things or people together developed into the legal sense of binding parties by agreement, while physical drawing together produced the sense of shrinking or tightening. The disease sense developed from the idea of acquiring or taking an illness upon oneself.

note.ja: 当事者間の合意を広く表すが、すべての agreement が法的に強制可能な contract になるとは限らない。
note.en: A broad term for mutual understanding; not every agreement constitutes a legally enforceable contract.

note.ja: 契約・証書に含まれる、行為または不作為についての正式で厳格な約束。
note.en: A formal and serious promise, often contained in a contract or deed, to act or refrain from acting.

note.ja: 義務の履行や一定の行為について与える正式な約束・確約。
note.en: A formal promise or assurance to perform an obligation or take a particular action.

note.ja: 物の大きさ・体積などが小さくなることを表す一般語で、物理的意味の contract に近い。
note.en: A general verb for becoming smaller in size or volume, corresponding to the physical sense of contract.

note.en: Means obtaining a disease, characteristic, or right; acquire an infection may sound more technical than contract an infection.

usage.consensus: Uncountable agreement means a shared opinion or the state of accepting the same position.
usage.arrangement: A countable agreement is a particular arrangement under which parties accept specified terms.
usage.document: Agreement may also refer to the written document recording the parties’ arrangement.
usage.legal_effect: Some agreements are legally enforceable contracts, while others are social, political, preliminary, or otherwise non-binding.
usage.prepositions: Use between for the participating parties, with for the other party, and on or about for the subject matter.
usage.infinitive: Agreement to do identifies an action that the parties have accepted: an agreement to supply goods.
usage.grammar_sense: In grammar, agreement means correspondence between related words in features such as number, person, or gender.

an arrangement containing terms or promises accepted by the parties
a contract or formal instrument establishing rights and obligations
a written document recording what the parties have agreed

nuance.ja: agreement は「同意している状態」から、具体的な取り決め、さらにその内容を記載した文書までを広く表す。contract は通常、法律上強制可能な権利・義務を生じさせる合意に焦点を置くが、agreement は友人同士の非公式な約束や政治的合意など、法的拘束力のないものも含み得る。したがって、Every contract is an agreement, but not every agreement is a contract. という整理が一般的に可能である。ただし、文書の表題が Agreement か Contract かだけで法的拘束力が決まるわけではない。in agreement は「同意して」、reach an agreement は「協議の結果、合意に達する」を意味する。文法では subject-verb agreement のように、語形の数・人称などの一致を表す。
nuance.en: Agreement broadly covers the state of agreeing, a particular arrangement, and the document recording that arrangement. Contract normally focuses on an agreement that creates legally enforceable rights or obligations, whereas agreement may also include an informal understanding between friends or a political arrangement without legal force. It is therefore generally possible to say that every contract is an agreement, but not every agreement is a contract. The title Agreement or Contract does not by itself determine whether a document is legally binding. In agreement means sharing the same view, while reach an agreement emphasizes successful completion of negotiation. In grammar, agreement describes correspondence in features such as number and person, as in subject-verb agreement.

ja: agreement：当事者間の合意・取り決めを広く表し、法的拘束力を持つとは限らない。

an accord is a formal agreement, often reached after disagreement or diplomatic negotiation.
consensus is an opinion or judgment broadly shared within a group.
consent is voluntary approval of a particular proposal, act, or request.
a settlement is an agreement that resolves a dispute, lawsuit, or claim.

etymology.ja: agreement は動詞 agree に、状態・結果・行為を表す接尾辞 -ment が付いて成立した。agree は古フランス語 agreer「喜ばせる、満足させる、同意する」に由来し、これは句 a gré「好みに、意にかなって」と関係する。gré はラテン語 gratus「喜ばしい、ありがたい」にさかのぼる。相手の提案が意にかなうという発想から、「同意する」「意見が一致する」という意味が発達した。
etymology.en: Agreement was formed from the verb agree with the noun-forming suffix -ment, which denotes a state, act, or result. Agree came from Old French agreer, meaning to please, satisfy, or consent, and is related to the phrase a gré, according to one’s pleasure. Gré ultimately derives from Latin gratus, pleasing or welcome. The idea that another person’s proposal was acceptable or pleasing developed into the meanings consent and hold the same opinion.
